title: Angkor Wat International Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the 30th Edition Was Like
seo_title: Angkor Wat International Half Marathon 2026 Review
meta_description: Angkor Wat International Half Marathon review: a record 16,000 runners for the 30th edition on 7 December 2025, and a race founded to help landmine victims.
dek: The Angkor Wat International Half Marathon marked 30 years in December 2025 with a record 16,000 registered runners. Here is what that edition was like, ahead of 2026.
verdict: The Angkor Wat International Half Marathon is a race with a remarkable history. It was first organised in 1995 by UNTAC and Cambodia's National Olympic Committee to draw attention to landmines and help their victims [1]. The 30th edition, on 7 December 2025, drew a record 16,000 registered runners, about 10,000 Cambodians and more than 3,000 from abroad [1]. Money raised supports social programmes [1]. If you want a race with history, a cause and the Angkor temples as the setting, this is the one.

sections.heading: Thirty Years On
paragraphs: The race was first held in 1995, organised by UNTAC and the National Olympic Committee of Cambodia to focus global attention on landmines and support those injured by them [1]. In 1996 only about 300 runners took part [1].
Numbers reached 15,000 before the Covid-19 pandemic, fell afterwards and recovered to 14,000 in 2024 [1].

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: The 30th anniversary race was held around Angkor on 7 December 2025, with a record 16,000 registered participants [1]. About 10,000 were Cambodian runners and more than 3,000 came from abroad [1].

The National Olympic Committee's secretary general, Vath Chamroeun, described the event as at once a sporting event, a humanitarian effort and a way to show Cambodia to the world [1]. Funds raised support a range of social programmes [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want to run among the Angkor temples in a race with real history and purpose. The field keeps growing, so plan early.

Book accommodation in Siem Reap well ahead: with 16,000 runners plus family and friends, many staying several nights, the town fills up on race weekend [1]. The December date is in the cooler, dry season.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Angkor Wat International Half Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: A record 16,000 registered for the 30th edition on 7 December 2025: about 10,000 Cambodian runners and more than 3,000 international participants. In 2024 the race had 14,000.

faqs.question: Why was the Angkor Wat Half Marathon started?
faqs.answer: It was first organised in 1995 by UNTAC and Cambodia's National Olympic Committee to draw global attention to landmines and to help people whose lives had been shattered by them. Funds raised today support a range of social programmes.

faqs.question: When is the Angkor Wat International Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: In early December. The 30th edition was on 7 December 2025, and the 2026 edition is scheduled for 6 December 2026, around the Angkor temples near Siem Reap.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous edition (7 December 2025). Replaces a pre-race preview. The source was published on the eve of the race, quoting the organiser's final registration total. No rating.
